'''''Quanta Magazine''''' is an editorially independent<ref>{{cite web|title=About Quanta Magazine 
|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/about/|work=Quanta Magazine|publisher=Simons Foundation|access-date=6 November 2019}}</ref> [[online publication]] of the [[Simons Foundation]] covering developments in [[physics]], [[mathematics]], [[biology]] and [[computer science]].

==History==
''Quanta Magazine'' was initially launched as ''Simons Science News''<ref>{{cite news
|author=Dennis Overbye
|title=A Magazine or a Living Fossil? 
|url = https://www.nytimes.com/2013/05/07/science/a-glossy-science-magazine-or-living-fossil.html 
|work = The New York Times 
|date = 6 May 2013
|access-date = 6 November 2019}}</ref> in October 2012, but it was renamed to its current title in July 2013.<ref>{{cite news
|author=Carl Zimmer
|author-link=Carl Zimmer
|title=How Things Get Complex: My New Story for Scientific American & Quanta Magazine |url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/science/phenomena/2013/07/17/how-things-get-complex-my-new-story-for-scientific-american-quanta-magazine/
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826052037/https://www.nationalgeographic.com/science/phenomena/2013/07/17/how-things-get-complex-my-new-story-for-scientific-american-quanta-magazine/
|url-status=dead
|archive-date=August 26, 2018
|publisher=National Geographic 
|access-date=6 November 2019}}</ref>

It was founded by the former ''[[New York Times]]'' journalist Thomas Lin, who was the magazine's [[editor-in-chief]] until 2024.<ref>{{cite news
|title=Reinventing The Boundaries of Science Journalism 
|author = Jonathan Wai
|url=https://www.psychologytoday.com/blog/finding-the-next-einstein/201406/reinventing-the-boundaries-science-journalism 
|publisher=[[Psychology Today]]
|date=16 June 2014
|access-date=6 November 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news
|title=Quanta Magazine's Thomas Lin Spends His Days 'Illuminating Science' 
|author = Kara Bloomgarden-Smoke
|url=http://observer.com/2016/05/quanta-magazines-thomas-lin/ 
|publisher=Observer 
|date=20 May 2016
|access-date=6 November 2019}}</ref> The deputy editor is Michael Moyer, formerly of ''[[Scientific American]]'', and the art director is Samuel Velasco.  In 2024, Samir Patel became the magazine's second editor in chief.<ref>{{cite news
|author=Thomas Lin
|author-link=Thomas Lin
|title= My Fantastic Voyage at Quanta Magazine |url= https://www.quantamagazine.org/my-fantastic-voyage-at-quanta-magazine-20240412/
|publisher=Quanta Magazine 
|access-date=12 May 2024}}</ref>

==Content==
The articles in the magazine are freely available to read online.<ref>{{cite web |author=Richard Elwes |date=6 November 2013 |title=Quanta Magazine |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/editorial/quanta-magazine |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 November 2019 |publisher=London Mathematical Society}}</ref> ''[[Scientific American]]'',<ref>{{cite news|title=Stories by Quanta Magazine|url=http://www.scientificamerican.com/author/quanta-magazine/|access-date=6 November 2019|work=Scientific American}}</ref> [[Wired (magazine)|''Wired'']],<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Quanta Magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/tag/quanta-magazine/|access-date=6 November 2019|magazine=Wired}}</ref> ''[[The Atlantic]]'', and ''[[The Washington Post]]'', as well as international science publications like ''[[Spektrum der Wissenschaft]]'',<ref>{{cite news|title=Quanta Magazine|url=http://www.spektrum.de/index/quanta-magazine-auf-deutsch/1436462|access-date=6 November 2019|work=Spektrum der Wissenschaft}}</ref> have reprinted articles from the magazine. Articles from the magazine have been translated into German, Spanish, French, Chinese, Italian and Japanese.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About Quanta Magazine |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/about/ |access-date=2025-06-30 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref>

In November 2018, [[MIT Press]] published two collections of articles from ''Quanta Magazine'', ''Alice and Bob Meet the Wall of Fire''<ref>{{cite book
 |editor= Thomas Lin
 |year= 2018
 |title= Alice and Bob Meet the Wall of Fire: The Biggest Ideas in Science from Quanta [''sic'']
 |url= https://mitpress.mit.edu/books/alice-and-bob-meet-wall-fire
 |location= Cambridge, Massachusetts
 |publisher= MIT Press
 |isbn= 9780262536349
}}</ref> and ''The Prime Number Conspiracy''.<ref>{{cite book
 |editor= Thomas Lin
 |year= 2018
 |title= The Prime Number Conspiracy: The Biggest Ideas in Math from Quanta [''sic'']
 |url= https://mitpress.mit.edu/books/prime-number-conspiracy
 |location= Cambridge, Massachusetts
 |publisher= MIT Press
 |isbn= 9780262536356
}}</ref>

The magazine's YouTube channel has more than one million subscribers and publishes award-winning animated explainer videos and short documentaries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quanta Magazine |url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCTpmmkp1E4nmZqWPS-dl5bg |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=YouTube |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Winners |url=https://www.tellyawards.com/winners/2022/non-broadcast/general-not-for-profit/ |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=Telly Awards |language=en-US}}</ref>

The magazine also has three podcasts, two of which are hosted by [[Steven Strogatz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quanta Magazine's Science and Math Podcasts |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/podcasts/ |access-date=2024-10-19 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref> [[Janna Levin]] joined as cohost of ''The Joy of Why'' for the third season in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-25 |title=Janna Levin: Why I'm Co-Hosting the Joy of Why Podcast |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/janna-levin-why-im-co-hosting-the-joy-of-why-podcast-20240125/ |access-date=2024-10-20 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref>

==Reception==
''[[Undark Magazine]]'' described ''Quanta Magazine'' as "highly regarded for its masterful coverage of complex topics in science and math."<ref>{{cite news|title=Hard-Sciences Magazine Goes to the Next Level|author=Robin Lloyd|url=https://undark.org/2017/05/04/hard-sciences-magazine-goes-next-level/|date=5 April 2017|access-date=6 November 2019|work=Undark Magazine}}</ref> The science news aggregator ''RealClearScience'' ranked ''Quanta Magazine'' first on its list of "The Top 10 Websites for Science in 2018."<ref>{{cite news|title=The Top 10 Websites for Science in 2018|author=Ross Pomeroy|url=https://www.realclearscience.com/blog/2018/12/10/the_top_10_websites_for_science_in_2018.html|publisher =RealClearScience|date=2018-12-10|access-date=6 November 2019}}</ref>

In 2020, the magazine received a National Magazine Award for General Excellence from the [[American Society of Magazine Editors]] for its "willingness to tackle some of the toughest and most difficult topics in science and math in a language that is accessible to the lay reader without condescension or [[oversimplification]]."

In May 2022, the magazine's staff, notably [[Natalie Wolchover]], were awarded the [[Pulitzer Prize for Explanatory Reporting]] for an article Wolchover wrote about the [[James Webb Space Telescope]] and an accompanying short documentary by Emily Buder.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The 2022 Pulitzer Prize Winner in Explanatory Reporting |url=https://www.pulitzer.org/winners/staff-quanta-magazine-new-york-ny-notably-natalie-wolchover |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=www.pulitzer.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pulitzer.org/news/2022-pulitzer-prize-announcement|title=The 2022 Pulitzer Prize Announcement|website=pulitzer.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=shPwW11MEHg |title=How NASA's Webb Telescope Will Transform Our Place in the Universe |date=2021-12-03 |last=Quanta Magazine |access-date=2025-06-21 |via=YouTube}}</ref>
